openwrt_wiki.Einleitung: The NETGEAR AC1600 Smart WiFi Router is a router delivering AC1600 WiFi (2.4 & 5 GHz) and Gigabit Ethernet speeds. It features five 10/100/1000 (1 WAN and 4 LAN) Gigabit Ethernet ports with auto-sensing technology, one USB 2.0 port and is powered by a 880MHz MIPS32el processor, 128 MiB RAM and a 128 MiB NAND Flash. It is fully functional under OpenWrt.
openwrt_wiki.Verwandte Geräte: This device uses the same OEM firmware as other two (R6350 and R6850) ... It appears that the PCB is identical, the main difference seems to be in the external antennas.
openwrt_wiki.Hinweis WLAN: Some devices have an issue with wireless and need a patched kernel to correctly read calibration data from Flash, but it is unknown how common this is.
openwrt_wiki.Installation OEM: Apply factory OpenWrt image via OEM web-gui. You may be prompted to confirm that the version would be a downgrade, accept to continue flashing. If after flashing OpenWrt you still see the OEM ROM, flash OpenWrt again.
openwrt_wiki.Installation NMRP: nmrpflash for both installation and recovery; connect to LAN1 port (does not work on WAN); nmrpflash -i <interface> -f openwrt-ramips-mt7621-netgear_r6260-squashfs-factory.img; expects factory image format (*-factory.img or OEM).
openwrt_wiki.Flash Layout: raw NAND flash (MX30LF1G18AC-TI) 128MiB: mtd0 u-boot 1 MiB | mtd1 SC PART_MAP 1 MiB | mtd2 kernel 4 MiB | mtd3 ubi 40 MiB | mtd4 reserved0 24 MiB | mtd5 factory 2 MiB | mtd6 reserved1 56 MiB; reserved0 = language translations (12 partitions), reserved1 = additional 12 partitions
openwrt_wiki.Debricking: U-Boot in ROM with TFTP and Serial upload; UART requires opening the enclosure, soldering a 4-pin header and two bridges (TX/RX), 3v3 logic. Menu 1: TFTP to SDRAM, 2: TFTP then write to Flash, 3: boot from Flash (default), 4: boot command line, 7: bootloader via Serial, 9: bootloader via TFTP. Defaults: TFTP server 10.10.10.3, self 10.10.10.123, filename test.bin
openwrt_wiki.Netzwerk: br-lan 192.168.1.1/24; eth0 DSA master; lan1 = LAN port 1 (closest to WAN) .. lan4; wan = WAN port (yellow, labeled Internet), DHCP; wlan0 2.4 GHz radio0, wlan1 5 GHz radio1
openwrt_wiki.Switch-Ports: Internet (WAN) p4, LAN1 p3, LAN2 p2, LAN3 p1, LAN4 p0 (Inversion); OpenWrt names lan1..lan4 match the labels
openwrt_wiki.Gehäuse öffnen: Remove three T10 screws, two of them are under the bottom rubber pads. The top has plastic clips along the perimeter which can be unclipped sequentially and a single tab at the back end which slides out once all clips are unhooked. The PCB is secured with a single screw (top left) which only needs to be slightly loosened and the PCB can then be pulled forward to remove.
openwrt_wiki.Seriell: The UART is a 4-pin header under the WAN port. It is labeled J4 and the pin-out is GND, TX, 3v3, RX (pins 1-4). It uses 3v3 logic, but is neither populated nor are the corresponding resistors included. In order to use the UART header two of the missing resistors must be bridged (R53 and R54). 57600, 8N1
openwrt_wiki.JTAG: See JTAG section for R6350 - the PCB looks the same, but the JTAG functionality has not been confirmed.

openwrt_git.titel: ramips: add support for Netgear R6260 and R6850
openwrt_git.text: As Netgear uses the same image for R6260, R6350 & R6850 we can merge device tree files and generate separate images for each device. [add missing WiFi compatible string, fix network configuration]

openwrt_git_factory.titel: ramips: add factory image for Netgear R6350
openwrt_git_factory.text: This adds factory image generation for all three devices. These images can be flashed via WebUI for easy installation.

openwrt_git_eeprom.titel: ramips: fix NETGEAR R6260 EEPROM offset
openwrt_git_eeprom.text: The EEPROM offset for the NETGEAR R6260 is incorrect, thus no valid calibration data is used.
openwrt_git_eeprom.revert: Netgear seems to use different partition layouts on the R6260, which would require us to dynamically detect the position of (at least) the factory partition. Revert this fix to avoid breaking existing installations until a better solution has been worked out.

openwrt_git_partitionen.titel: ramips: use on-flash partition table for Sercomm BZV/CHJ
openwrt_git_partitionen.text: These devices have a partition table stored in flash, which compensates for any pre-existing bad blocks by enlarging the respective partition. This means that the current static partition table is only correct for devices without any bad blocks. Typical results of this mismatch are degraded wireless performance and wrong MAC addresses, when the factory partition is shifted due to a bad block somewhere before it. If there is a bad block already before the ubi partition, then OpenWrt may not run at all because the kernel can't find the rootfs. Use the on-flash partition table to fix these issues.

Text: "CHJ00D-1.6" is silkscreened on the board in the FCC photos.
The radio chip IDs are not visible in the FCC internal photos but MT7603E + MT7615? seems like a reasonable guess.
The 5GHz chip appears to be wired for four spatial streams but the fourth is not connected to any antenna and would likely be disabled in software limiting this device to three spatial streams.
The Netgear WAC124 uses the same board but has all four spatial streams implemented making it an AC2000 product.
